title: 돌발 주제 모음
intro: 돌발 주제는 서베이에서 고르지 않은 날씨·교통·재활용·휴대폰·인터넷·명절·가구·은행 같은 일상 주제가 갑자기 나오는 문제입니다. 당황하지 말고 '가족과 서울에 사는 경영학과 3학년 대학생'이라는 내 페르소나 시점으로 답하면 됩니다. 지하철 30분 통학, 10층 아파트, 내 방 책상, 친구 Minji처럼 이미 준비한 디테일을 그대로 끌어오면 어떤 주제든 금방 이야기가 됩니다.
strategy: 답변 흐름: 시작 문장('Oh, ~? Let me think.') → 기본 정보(한국은/우리 집은) → 내 일상·세부(지하철, 우리 아파트, 가족) → 느낌·이유 → 마무리 문장('Yeah, that's ~.')
처음 보는 주제라도 첫 문장은 시간을 버는 'Oh, ~? That's an interesting question. Let me think.' 로 고정하세요.
주제를 내 페르소나로 끌어오세요: 교통 → 지하철 30분 통학, 가구 → 내 방 책상, 인터넷 → 넷플릭스·과제, 명절 → 가족과 추석.
비교(comparison) 문제는 '예전에는 ~ → 요즘은 ~ → 내 생각' 순서로, 경험(experience) 문제는 과거시제로 언제 → 무슨 일 → 결과를 말합니다.

expressions.en: Oh, that's an interesting question. Let me think.
expressions.note: 돌발 주제 만능 시작 문장. 시간 벌기용

expressions.en: In Korea, we have four seasons.
It takes about thirty minutes by subway.
I use my phone for pretty much everything.
expressions.ko: 저는 거의 모든 걸 휴대폰으로 해요.

expressions.en: We separate plastic, paper, and cans.
I usually spend time with my family.
It was a little stressful at first.
When I was younger, I used to ~.
I can't imagine my life without it.
expressions.ko: 그것 없는 생활은 상상이 안 돼요.

expressions.en: It turned out to be a simple mistake.
expressions.note: turn out to be = 알고 보니 ~였다

expressions.en: It's become such a big part of my daily life.
expressions.ko: 그게 제 일상에서 정말 큰 부분이 됐어요.

expressions.en: So yeah, that's pretty much how it is for me.

questions.en: Tell me about the weather in your country. What are the seasons like, and which season do you like the most?
questions.ko: 당신 나라의 날씨에 대해 말해 주세요. 계절은 어떤가요? 그리고 어떤 계절을 가장 좋아하나요?
tips: 답변 흐름: 'Oh, the weather in Korea? Let me think.' → 사계절 소개 → 각 계절 한두 문장 → 내가 좋아하는 계절과 이유(한강 조깅) → 'Yeah, that's ~.'
계절마다 hot and humid / cold and dry / warm / cool 같은 쉬운 형용사만 써도 충분합니다.
좋아하는 계절 이유를 내 일상(저녁 조깅, 공원 산책)과 연결하면 IH 이상이 됩니다.

answers.IM3: Oh, the weather in Korea? Let me think. In Korea, we have four seasons. Spring is warm, and there are a lot of flowers. Summer is really hot and humid, and it rains a lot. Fall is cool and sunny. Winter is very cold and dry. My favorite season is fall. The weather is perfect for jogging along the Han River in the evening. Yeah, that's the weather in Korea.
answers.IH: Oh, the weather in Korea? Let me think. In Korea, we have four clear seasons. Spring is warm and nice, and there are cherry blossoms everywhere. The only bad thing is the fine dust. Summer is really hot and humid, and we have a rainy season in July. Fall is cool and sunny, and the leaves turn red and yellow. Winter is very cold and dry, and it sometimes snows in Seoul. My favorite season is definitely fall. I go jogging along the Han River three times a week, and in fall, it's not too hot or too cold. The sky is so clear, and the trees in the park near my apartment look really pretty. Also, it's great weather for hanging out with friends outside. Yeah, that's why I really like fall.
answers.AL: Oh, the weather in Korea? That's an interesting question. Let me think. Well, Korea has four pretty distinct seasons, and each one has its own charm. Spring is warm and lovely, and the whole city is covered in cherry blossoms, although the fine dust can be really annoying some days. Summer is a different story. It's super hot and sticky, and during the rainy season in July, it feels like it never stops pouring. Fall is cool, sunny, and dry, and the trees turn beautiful shades of red and yellow. Then winter comes, and it gets freezing cold, especially when the wind blows. If I had to pick one, it would definitely be fall. I go jogging along the Han River about three times a week, and in fall, the air is just perfect, not too hot and not too cold. After a long day of classes, running by the river while the sun goes down really clears my head. Plus, it's the best season for walking around the little park near my apartment or sitting outside at a cafe with my friend Minji. So yeah, that's why fall is my favorite season.

questions.en: How do you usually get around in your city? Tell me about the public transportation you use and what a typical trip is like.
questions.ko: 당신은 도시에서 보통 어떻게 이동하나요? 이용하는 대중교통과 평소 이동이 어떤지 말해 주세요.
tips: 답변 흐름: 'Sure, let me tell you about how I get around.' → 주로 지하철 이용 → 통학 루틴(역까지 5분, 학교까지 30분) → 지하철에서 하는 일(이어폰으로 IU) → 좋은 점·불편한 점 → 'Yeah, that's ~.'
routine 문제는 현재시제 + usually / every morning / on weekends 로 습관을 말합니다.
교통카드, 환승, 출퇴근 시간 혼잡 같은 디테일을 하나 넣으면 IH 이상이 됩니다.

answers.IM3: Sure, let me tell you about how I get around. I usually take the subway. The station is only five minutes from my apartment. It takes about thirty minutes to get to my school. In the morning, the subway is really crowded. But I just put on my earphones and listen to K-pop or IU songs. The subway in Seoul is clean, fast, and cheap. Yeah, that's how I usually get around.
answers.IH: Sure, let me tell you about how I get around in Seoul. I usually take the subway, because it's fast and cheap. Luckily, the station is only a five-minute walk from my apartment. On weekdays, I leave home around eight and get to school in about thirty minutes. I don't have to transfer, which is really nice. In the morning, the subway is so crowded that I usually can't sit down. So I just stand by the door, put on my earphones, and listen to IU or some ballads. Sometimes I check my class notes on my phone, too. I just tap my card when I get on, so it's really simple. On weekends, I sometimes ride a bike to the Han River instead. Yeah, that's how I usually get around.
answers.AL: Sure, I'd love to talk about how I get around. Honestly, I take the subway for pretty much everything, because Seoul's subway system is fast, clean, and super cheap. I'm lucky that the station is just a five-minute walk from my apartment, so I can leave home at the last minute and still make it. On weekdays, I take the same line straight to school, and it's about a thirty-minute ride with no transfers, which saves me a lot of stress. The only downside is rush hour. In the morning, the trains are so packed that I can barely move, let alone find a seat. So I just squeeze in by the door, put in my earphones, and listen to IU or some ballads. It's kind of my little moment of peace before a busy day of classes. On the way home, it's usually less crowded, so I sometimes sit down and catch up on my readings or text my friend Minji about our plans. On weekends, when the weather's nice, I ride my bike to the Han River instead, since it only takes ten minutes. So yeah, that's pretty much how I get around in the city.

questions.en: Tell me about recycling in your country. How does it work, and what do you do at home to recycle?
questions.ko: 당신 나라의 재활용에 대해 말해 주세요. 어떻게 이루어지고, 집에서는 재활용을 위해 무엇을 하나요?
tips: 답변 흐름: 'Oh, recycling? Let me think.' → 한국은 분리수거가 엄격하다 → 우리 아파트의 분리수거 방법(요일·장소) → 우리 가족이 하는 일(나와 남동생 담당) → 느낌·이유 → 'Yeah, that's ~.'
plastic, paper, cans, glass, food waste 다섯 단어만 알면 충분합니다.
'My brother and I take turns.' 처럼 가족 페르소나를 넣으면 이야기가 살아납니다.

answers.IM3: Oh, recycling? Let me think. In Korea, recycling is really important. We have to separate our trash. At home, we separate plastic, paper, cans, and glass. We also have a special bag for food waste. In my apartment complex, we take out the recycling every Wednesday. My younger brother and I usually do it together. It's a little annoying, but it's good for the environment. Yeah, that's how we recycle at home.
answers.IH: Oh, recycling? Let me think. In Korea, recycling is a really big deal, and the rules are pretty strict. Everyone has to separate their trash into plastic, paper, cans, glass, and food waste. If you don't, you might have to pay a fine. At home, we keep a few boxes on our small balcony, one for each type of recycling. My mom is really careful about it, so she always tells us to wash the plastic containers and take off the labels first. In my apartment complex, recycling day is every Wednesday evening. My younger brother Junho and I take turns carrying everything down to the parking lot. To be honest, it's a little annoying, especially after a long day at school. But I think it's worth it, because it's good for the environment. Yeah, that's how recycling works at my house.
answers.AL: Oh, recycling? That's an interesting one. Let me think. Well, in Korea, recycling is taken really seriously, and the rules are pretty strict compared to a lot of other countries. Basically, everyone has to sort their trash into plastic, paper, cans, glass, and food waste, and general trash has to go into special bags that you buy. If you mess it up, you can actually get fined. At my place, we have a little recycling station set up on our balcony, with separate boxes for each type. My mom is the boss when it comes to this. She always reminds us to rinse out the plastic containers and peel off the labels before we toss them in, and she'll totally call us out if we forget. In our apartment complex, recycling day is every Wednesday evening, so my younger brother Junho and I take turns carrying all the boxes down to the parking lot. Honestly, it's kind of a hassle when I get home late from school, and Junho and I argue about whose turn it is all the time. But I know it really helps the environment, so I don't mind that much. So yeah, that's pretty much how recycling works for my family.

questions.en: How has the way people use phones changed over the years? How is it different from when you were younger?
questions.ko: 사람들이 휴대폰을 사용하는 방식은 수년간 어떻게 변했나요? 당신이 어렸을 때와 어떻게 다른가요?
tips: 답변 흐름: 'Oh, phones? Let me think.' → 어렸을 때(전화·문자 위주, 부모님 폰) → 요즘(모든 걸 폰으로: 지하철 음악, 과제, 결제) → 내 생각(편리하지만 너무 많이 쓴다) → 'Yeah, that's ~.'
과거는 'When I was younger, I used to ~', 현재는 'These days, ~' 로 시제를 분명히 구분하세요.
IH 이상은 장점과 단점을 하나씩 말하고 내 생각으로 마무리하세요.

answers.IM3: Oh, phones? Let me think. When I was younger, people only used phones to call or text. I got my first phone in middle school, and it was pretty simple. These days, it's totally different. I use my phone for pretty much everything. I listen to music on the subway, watch videos, and do my school work. I even pay for my coffee with my phone. It's really convenient. Yeah, that's how phones have changed.
answers.IH: Oh, how phones have changed? Let me think. When I was in elementary school, my mom had a simple phone, and she only used it to call or send short text messages. We didn't really use phones for fun. I got my first smartphone in middle school, and it felt like magic. These days, it's totally different. People use their phones for pretty much everything. For example, I listen to music on the subway every morning, watch Netflix, and chat with my friend Minji all day. I also check my class schedule and even pay for things with my phone. It's really convenient, but I think people use their phones too much now. On the subway, everyone is just looking down at their screens. Sometimes I try to put mine away at dinner with my family. Yeah, that's how phone use has changed.
answers.AL: Oh, how phones have changed? That's an interesting question. Let me think. When I was a little kid, phones were really just for calling and texting. I remember my mom had a tiny flip phone, and she would only use it to call my dad or send him short messages. Nobody was glued to their screen back then. I got my first smartphone in middle school, and honestly, it felt like I had the whole world in my hand. These days, though, it's a completely different story. Phones have become such a big part of daily life that I can't imagine going a day without mine. I use it to listen to IU on the subway, watch Netflix in bed, check my class announcements, and chat with Minji pretty much all day. I even pay for my iced Americano with my phone. It's super convenient, no doubt about that. But at the same time, I feel like people are kind of addicted now. On the subway, literally everyone is staring at their screens, and nobody talks to each other. That's why my family has a little rule that we don't use our phones during dinner. So yeah, that's how the way we use phones has changed.

questions.en: What do you usually do on the internet? Tell me about the websites or apps you use most and when you use them.
questions.ko: 당신은 인터넷으로 보통 무엇을 하나요? 가장 많이 쓰는 웹사이트나 앱, 그리고 언제 사용하는지 말해 주세요.
tips: 답변 흐름: 'Sure, let me tell you about ~.' → 인터넷을 거의 매일 쓴다 → 시간대별 사용(아침 지하철 음악앱, 낮 과제·학교 사이트, 밤 넷플릭스) → 가장 좋아하는 앱과 이유 → 'Yeah, that's ~.'
routine 문제는 in the morning / during the day / at night 처럼 시간 순서로 말하면 쉽습니다.
브랜드 이름보다 'a music app', 'a video app', 'my school website' 처럼 쉬운 설명을 함께 쓰세요.

answers.IM3: Sure, let me tell you about what I do online. I use the internet every day. In the morning, I listen to music on a music app on the subway. At school, I use my school website to check my classes and turn in my homework. At night, I watch movies on Netflix. I also chat with my friends on a messenger app. Yeah, that's what I usually do on the internet.
answers.IH: Sure, let me tell you about what I usually do online. Honestly, I use the internet all day long. In the morning, I open a music app on the subway and listen to K-pop and ballads, especially IU. During the day, I use my school website a lot. I check my class schedule, download lecture notes, and turn in my assignments there. When I work on group projects, I also search for information and share files with my classmates. At night, after dinner, I usually watch something on Netflix, like a comedy or an action movie. And of course, I chat with my friend Minji on a messenger app all the time. The app I use the most is probably Netflix, because it helps me relax after a busy day. Yeah, that's what I usually do on the internet.
answers.AL: Sure, I'd love to talk about that. To be honest, I'm online pretty much from the moment I wake up until I go to bed. In the morning, the first thing I do on the subway is open my music app and put on some IU or ballads. It's kind of my way of waking up. During the day, my school website is my best friend, whether I like it or not. That's where I check announcements, download lecture slides, and submit assignments, usually right before the deadline. Since I'm a business major, I also have tons of group projects, so I'm always searching for data online and sharing files with my teammates. Then, at night, I finally get to relax. I usually watch a comedy or an action movie on Netflix, and on weekends, I sometimes binge-watch a whole series. On top of that, I'm constantly chatting with my friend Minji on a messenger app, mostly about where to eat or which cafe to try next. If I had to pick the app I use most, it'd definitely be Netflix, since it's how I unwind after a long, busy day. So yeah, that's pretty much what my online life looks like.

questions.en: Tell me about a memorable holiday you celebrated, like Chuseok or New Year's. What did you do, who were you with, and why was it special?
questions.ko: 추석이나 설날처럼 기억에 남는 명절에 대해 말해 주세요. 무엇을 했고, 누구와 함께였으며, 왜 특별했나요?
tips: 답변 흐름: 'Oh, a memorable holiday? Let me think.' → 언제(작년 추석) → 누구와(엄마·아빠·남동생 Junho, 조부모님) → 무엇을 했는지(송편, 음식, 영화) → 왜 특별했는지 → 'Yeah, that's ~.'
경험 문제는 과거시제를 끝까지 유지하세요. made / ate / watched / stayed up.
특별했던 이유를 하나의 장면(할머니와 송편 빚기)으로 생생하게 묘사하면 AL에 가까워집니다.

answers.IM3: Oh, a memorable holiday? Let me think. I remember last Chuseok really well. My family and I visited my grandparents. We made songpyeon together. My younger brother's songpyeon looked really funny, so we laughed a lot. We also ate a lot of delicious food. At night, we watched a movie together on TV. It was special because my whole family was together all day. Yeah, that's my most memorable holiday.
answers.IH: Oh, a memorable holiday? Let me think. The one I remember best is last Chuseok. Usually, my life is pretty busy with classes, so I don't see my grandparents very often. But during Chuseok, my parents, my younger brother Junho, and I drove to my grandparents' house. The traffic was terrible, and it took almost five hours! When we got there, my grandmother had already made a lot of food. In the afternoon, we all sat on the floor and made songpyeon together. Junho's songpyeon looked so weird that everyone laughed for a long time. In the evening, we ate dinner and watched a funny movie on TV. It was special because we don't usually spend a whole day together like that. Yeah, that's why last Chuseok is my most memorable holiday.
answers.AL: Oh, a memorable holiday? That's a nice question. Let me think. I'd have to say last Chuseok. My weekdays are usually so packed with classes and group projects that I barely get to see my grandparents, so I was really looking forward to it. Early in the morning, my parents, my younger brother Junho, and I squeezed into the car and drove down to my grandparents' house. The traffic was a total nightmare, and a three-hour drive ended up taking almost five. But the moment we walked in, the whole house smelled like my grandmother's cooking, and I forgot all about the long ride. In the afternoon, we all sat around a big table and made songpyeon together. My grandmother kept showing me how to fold them nicely, while Junho's came out looking like little rocks, and we couldn't stop laughing. That evening, after a huge dinner, we all lay on the floor and watched a comedy movie on TV, and my grandfather fell asleep halfway through. It was such a simple day, but it felt really special, because we hardly ever get to slow down and just be together like that. So yeah, that's my most memorable holiday.

questions.en: Tell me about your favorite piece of furniture in your home. What does it look like, where is it, and why do you like it?
questions.ko: 집에서 가장 좋아하는 가구에 대해 말해 주세요. 어떻게 생겼고, 어디에 있으며, 왜 좋아하나요?
tips: 답변 흐름: 'Oh, my favorite furniture? Let me think.' → 무엇인지(내 방 책상) → 어디에 있고 어떻게 생겼는지(창가, 흰색, 노트북) → 그 위에서 하는 일 → 좋아하는 이유 → 'Yeah, that's ~.'
describe 문제는 크기·색깔·위치를 먼저 말한 뒤 내가 하는 일로 넘어가면 자연스럽습니다.
'I've had it for ~ years.' 로 이 집에서 산 10년과 연결하면 페르소나가 이어집니다.

answers.IM3: Oh, my favorite furniture? Let me think. My favorite piece of furniture is the desk in my room. It's next to the window, so it gets a lot of sunlight. It's white and pretty big. I keep my laptop, some books, and a small lamp on it. I study and do my homework there every day. I also watch movies on my laptop there. Yeah, that's why I really like my desk.
answers.IH: Oh, my favorite piece of furniture? Let me think. I'd say it's the desk in my room. My room isn't very big. There's just a bed, a desk, and a small bookshelf. But my desk is right next to the window, so it gets a lot of sunlight in the afternoon. It's white and wide, and it has two drawers on the side. I keep my laptop, a small lamp, and some photos of my friends on it. My parents bought it for me when we moved into this apartment about ten years ago, so I've used it since elementary school. These days, I spend hours there doing assignments for my business classes. At night, I also watch Netflix on my laptop at my desk. Yeah, that's why my desk is my favorite piece of furniture.
answers.AL: Oh, my favorite piece of furniture? That's an interesting question. Let me think. It would definitely be the desk in my room. My room is pretty small, with just a bed, a desk, and a little bookshelf, but the desk is kind of the heart of it. It's right by the window, so on sunny afternoons, the light pours in, and I can see the whole neighborhood from the tenth floor. It's a simple white desk, nice and wide, with a couple of drawers on the side where I stuff all my notes and chargers. On top, there's my laptop, a small lamp, and a few photos of me and my friend Minji. What makes it special is that my parents bought it for me when we moved into this apartment about ten years ago. So I've done everything there, from my elementary school homework to the business reports I'm working on now. During exam season, I practically live at that desk. And at night, when I'm done studying, I put on a comedy on my laptop and finally relax. It's seen me grow up, in a way. So yeah, that's why my desk means so much to me.

questions.en: Have you ever had a problem at a bank or with a banking app? Tell me what happened and how you solved it.
questions.ko: 은행이나 은행 앱에서 문제가 생긴 적이 있나요? 무슨 일이 있었고 어떻게 해결했는지 말해 주세요.
tips: 답변 흐름: 'Oh, a problem with a bank? Let me think.' → 언제(오사카 여행 전 환전, 또는 친구에게 송금) → 무슨 문제(앱이 잠김 / 잘못 송금) → 해결 과정(은행 방문, 고객센터 전화) → 결과·배운 점 → 'Yeah, that's ~.'
과거시제와 순서 표현(First / Then / In the end)으로 이야기를 정리하세요.
IH 이상은 내 감정(panicked, relieved)을 넣어 이야기를 생생하게 만드세요.

answers.IM3: Oh, a problem with a bank? Let me think. Last year, I wanted to send money to my friend Minji. We had dinner, and I paid her back with my banking app. But the app suddenly locked because I typed the wrong password too many times. I was so stressed! So I went to a bank near my school with my ID. The staff helped me, and it took about twenty minutes. Yeah, that's my bank story.
answers.IH: Oh, a problem with a bank? Let me think. Actually, it happened last year. My friend Minji and I had dinner at a nice restaurant near school, and she paid for both of us. So that night, I tried to send her my half with my banking app. But I couldn't remember my new password, and after five tries, the app locked me out. I panicked a little, because I also needed the app to pay my phone bill that week. The next day, I called the bank's customer service, but they said I had to visit a branch in person. So after my morning class, I went to a bank near the subway station with my ID card. The staff member was really kind, and she reset everything in about twenty minutes. I finally sent Minji the money. Now I write my passwords down somewhere safe. Yeah, that's how I solved my bank problem.
answers.AL: Oh, a problem with a bank? Let me think. Actually, I had a pretty stressful one last year. My friend Minji and I went out for dinner at this nice Italian place near campus, and she paid for both of us, so I promised to send her my half that night. When I got home, I opened my banking app, but I'd just changed my password the week before, and I couldn't remember it for the life of me. I tried a few different ones, and after the fifth wrong try, the app completely locked me out. I totally panicked, because my phone bill was due in two days, and I pay everything through that app. The next morning, I called customer service, hoping they could fix it over the phone, but it turned out I had to visit a branch in person with my ID. So right after my morning class, I rushed to the bank near my subway station. The staff member was super patient. She checked my ID, helped me set a new password, and had everything working again in about twenty minutes. I was so relieved that I sent Minji the money right there in the bank. Since then, I keep my passwords written down somewhere safe. So yeah, that's how I handled my bank app disaster.
